input.question: How do cycle life and low-temperature performance compare for stationary grid storage?

blocks.markdown:
## Direct Comparison and Available Evidence

The provided literature does not establish a direct performance comparison between sodium-ion batteries and lithium iron phosphate batteries for stationary grid storage under identical cycle-life testing or low-temperature conditions\. [5](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.04963)

At the cathode level, sodium-ion batteries are noted to be uncompetitive compared to high-energy lithium-ion systems such as those utilizing lithium cobalt oxide or lithium iron phosphate, although sodium-ion chemistry is anticipated to provide complementary solutions suited for stationary energy storage\. [5](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.04963)

## Cycle Life Characteristics

In general comparisons against the broader lithium-ion battery family, sodium-ion batteries suffer from lower gravimetric energy density and inferior cycle life, which remains a key challenge despite their potential utility in high-power stationary storage\. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.24683)

For lithium iron phosphate pouch cells, cycle degradation and operational lifespan are sensitive to thermal management interfaces; for instance, tests conducted at a 2C rate over 103 cycles showed that surface cooling yielded slower degradation than tab cooling, despite tab cooling providing better thermal homogeneity\. [4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10872)

Within sodium-ion research, phosphate-based polyanionic cathode materials demonstrate robust structural stability capable of thousands of cycles under specific conditions, such as Na3Fe2\(PO4\)\(P2O7\) retaining 89\.7% capacity after 6400 cycles at a 20C rate\. [6](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19299)

## Low-Temperature Performance and Limitations

Specific experimental evaluations of low-temperature performance for sodium-ion or lithium iron phosphate cells in stationary grid environments are not provided in the examined evidence\. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15440)

For lithium-ion batteries generally, low-temperature operation at 10 degrees Celsius exacerbates charge-transfer bottlenecks, induces severe overpotentials, and accelerates loss of lithium inventory, thereby significantly reducing projected service life compared to ambient conditions\. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15440)
